name: Macro tracking / IIFYM
lead: Macro tracking is the practice of logging daily grams of protein, carbohydrate and fat, rather than only total calories. "If It Fits Your Macros" (IIFYM) is the label for a flexible version in which any food is acceptable provided the targets are met. In looksmaxxing and fitness communities it is used to drive fat loss or muscle gain.[1]

Sources available for this entry are thin. Bodybuilding reference material describes protein, carbohydrate and fat as the three macronutrients whose ratios vary with an individual's goals, and notes that experts disagree on ideal protein amounts.[1] No clinical studies of IIFYM as a named approach were found.

paras: Users set gram targets for each macronutrient, typically with higher protein, and log food in an app. Energy is derived from roughly 4 kcal per gram of protein or carbohydrate and 9 kcal per gram of fat.[2] Bodybuilding literature notes protein recommendations ranging from about 25 to 30 percent of calories, with expert disagreement on the amount.[1]
Communities discuss macro targets as a refinement of calorie counting for cutting and bulking, particularly to retain muscle while losing facial fat.

card.summary: Tracking grams of protein, carbs and fat instead of just calories; common in cutting and bulking, little direct research.
card.note: No studies of IIFYM itself were found.

quick.overview:
Macro tracking means hitting daily targets for protein, carbs and fat. IIFYM is the flexible version where any food counts if the numbers fit.

It is a common method for gaining muscle or losing fat, but studies of IIFYM as such were not found.
quick.mechanism: Users log foods in an app against gram targets; total energy follows from standard energy factors per macronutrient.
quick.risks: Few direct risks are documented for the method itself. Experts disagree on ideal protein amounts, and logging accuracy depends on label estimates.
